The PCDAI success at p=0.02 suggests the clinical disease activity endpoint was more sensitive to the treatment effect. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was severely underpowered (N=22) for the primary histologic endpoint. The choice of CDHIS as primary endpoint may have been suboptimal — histologic healing may require longer treatment duration or may be less sensitive than clinical indices (PCDAI) for detecting GH effects. The mixed biomarker signals (CDEIS improved but calprotectin did not) suggest the mechanism partially engaged the intended biology. The partial outcome classification reflects: primary endpoint missed, secondary clinical endpoint met, biomarker signals mixed, and the trial was underpowered.

review_reason: The trial presents a complex partial outcome: primary histologic endpoint missed (no p-value reported, likely underpowered with N=22), but secondary clinical endpoint PCDAI met significance (p=0.02). Mixed biomarker signals (CDEIS improved, calprotectin did not) make it difficult to definitively classify the failure mode.
